newsitem.title: EGYPT: Three killed in Cairo shopping mall fire.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in Cairo shopping mall fire.

text.p: Three people were killed and 283 were injured when a fire caused by an electrical fault swept through a crowded shopping mall and cinema complex in Cairo overnight, officials said on Friday.

"There were a lot of women screaming and people started breaking glass to breathe. Everyone ran down the emergency stairs," said 16-year-old Adel Zaher, nursing a bandaged arm as he stood outside the eight-storey building watching rescue workers.
"I was standing around with my friends on the third floor and at first the lights went out. Then suddenly smoke came drifting up from downstairs."
Crowds outside the building shouted, whistled and pointed to direct rescue workers towards people stranded on the upper floors when the fire broke out on Thursday night.
Distraught relatives milled around the glass-littered streets trying to find family members. "My son, my son is in there," shouted one man, his hands on his head in distress.
Small explosions from the smoking rooftop sent sparks and glass flying over the side of the building and on to the streets below, showering crowds who stampeded in panic.
Assistant Interior Ministry official Raouf Menawi told Egyptian television on Friday that three people have died of their injuries and 283 people went to hospitals.
These included minor injuries and by mid-morning on Friday 56 people remained in hospitals, which reported that they had been treating people for burns and smoke inhalation.
Interior ministry officials said an electrical short circuit started the fire.
Ambulance driver Mohammad Osman said he had ferried at least 10 car loads of people suffering from smoke inhalation to nearby hospitals.
